newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore plans massive revamp of sewerage system.
newsitem.headline: Singapore plans massive revamp of sewerage system.

text.p: Singapore plans to build an island-wide network of deep tunnels and sewers to collect, treat and dispose all its waste water to minimise land use in sewage disposal, a Singapore official said on Friday.

Minister for the Environment Yeo Cheow Tong said the proposed Deep Tunnel Sewerage Scheme would eventually replace the country's six sewage treatment works with two new large ones, freeing up land for higher value-added developments.
Most of Singapore's existing sewerage facilities were now near major commercial or residential areas as a result of the city-state's rapid growth, Yeo said.
He was speaking at a contract signing ceremony for the appointment of a lead consultant for the new system.

He said a joint venture between CH2M Hill Cos Ltd and Parsons Brinckerhoff Consultants Pte Ltd had been awarded a Singapore $69.8 million (US$49.2 million) to be lead consultants in a feasibility study for the project.
The companies are expected to present the findings of their study and a preliminary design for the system in a year.
Under the system, treated waste currently discharged into the Johor Straits would be gradually reduced and eventually fully diverted through deep sea outfalls into the Singapore Straits, Yeo said.
